newsitem.title: USA: PacifiCorp to acquire Britain's Energy Group.
newsitem.headline: PacifiCorp to acquire Britain's Energy Group.

text.p: PacifiCorp said early on Friday it planned to acquire Britain's Energy Group Plc for $9.6 billion and would be selling its Pacific Telecom unit for $1.5 billion as part of the deal.
PacifiCorp, a diversified energy company in the U.S. and Australia, said it was paying 6.955 pounds sterling or $11.35 per share and would be assuming Energy Group's $3.8 billion of debt.

The boards of directors of both companies unanimously approved the transaction, valued at $9.6 billion in debt and equity, the company said. The deal is to be consummated by PacifiCorp's unit, PacifiCorp Holdings Inc.

In addition, PacifiCorp said it planned to shed its Pacific Telecom subsidiary to focus on the energy industry. It is selling the unit to Century Telephone Enterprises Inc for $1.5 billion in cash, plus assumption of Pacific Telecom debt.

"Pacific Telecom has been an important part of PacifiCorp's success for many years. However, our strategic focus is to become a leading global energy provider," President and Chief Executive Fred Buckman said in a statement. "This transaction focuses PacifiCorp squarely on the energy sector and will enable us to better meet the diversified energy needs of our customers."

Upon completion of the transaction, PacifiCorp will have 5 million electric and gas customers, 17,000 megawatts of generation capacity and more than 10 billion tons of coal reserves. Energy Group is an energy company in the United Kingdom, the United States and Australia.
Buckman will remain in his posts after the merger, as will Chief Financial Officer Richard O'Brien and General Counsel Verl Topham.
"This powerful combination positions the combined group as a premier global energy company with a significant presence on three continents," Buckman said in a statement.
PacifiCorp will acquire Energy Group through PacifiCorp Holdings Inc, which will finance the cash transaction initially through borrowings and the sale of its non-core assets, it said.
The offer is subject to regulatory approvals in the United Kingdom and to the conditions of the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Act in the United States.
The combined company will have a workforce of 26,000. The companies said they did not expect the combination to result in significant workforce reductions.
PacifiCorp said it also planned to sell other non-core assets, including PacifiCorp Financial Services and Pacific Generation Co.
Buckman said he was recommending that Energy Group Executive Chairman Derek Bonham and Chief Executive John Devaney join PacifiCorp's board of directors.
